District launched 1:1 with 1,800 iPads for every student K-12 in January 2014; USD 443 one-to-one initiative; govtech article referenced oversight of program
Elementary classrooms have iPad and Chromebook access; district has e-learning chromebook collection/return procedures; no firm launch year found in web sources
District provides each student personal device via 1:1 program; uses Google Classroom; no pre-2020 dated source found; 2020 CA distance learning program also referenced
Chromebooks distributed Jan 18-19 2017 at South Stokes HS; funded by Golden Leaf Foundation grant and Stokes County Commissioners matching funds; ~75% student take-up at launch
District has 1:1 device initiative; 2020 Operation Connectivity delivered 2,700 Chromebooks; no earlier firm launch year found in web sources
All students grades 7-12 assigned Chromebook; district uses ISD 885 Google suite; optional protection plan offered; no pre-2020 dated source found confirming launch year
Bond passed 2014 for $18.9M over 10 years; Chromebook cases distributed to grades 5-8 beginning 2016; program provides devices to grades 5-12; bond-funded 1:1 program likely launched fall 2015
Student-to-computer ratio of 1.1 (near 1:1); every classroom has interactive whiteboard; no specific launch year found in web sources; upper bound 2020
District has Chromebook program; no specific launch year or 1:1 announcement found in web sources; upper bound 2020
District implemented 1:1 Computing in 2017; grades 2-12 each assigned Chromebook for inside and outside classroom; K-1 have shared Chromebooks (1:Web)
Middle school (6-8) had 1:1 prior to COVID; expanded to HS during pandemic; district IT plan confirms pre-COVID 6-8 program; exact pre-COVID launch year not documented
Grades 9-12 received Chromebooks starting week of Aug 19 2019; earlier 5-12 program reported from 2015-16 for lower grades; HS expansion confirmed Feb 2019 board presentation
District technology page exists; no pre-2020 dated launch source found; upper bound 2020
First SLO County district to provide take-home devices for all 1,500 middle school (6-8) students in 2016; expanded to HS (grades 6-12; ~4,000 devices) in October 2017

Houston County Schools (HCBOE) separate from Dothan City Schools; HCBOE has device program (Connect Suite); no specific 1:1 launch year found in web sources; Dothan City began 1:1 with iPads in 2014-15 (different district)
Fort Mill School District (York 4) confirmed separate; York 02 is Rock Hill School District; district provides classroom access to Chrome tablets and Chromebooks; no specific 1:1 launch year found
District has Chromebook insurance program for student devices; serves Portland/Gresham area; no specific 1:1 program launch year found in web sources
Every student receives free iPad or Chromebook; no specific launch year found; district technology dept page references existing program; upper bound 2020

Pilot launched Feb 2015 in select 7th-8th grade classrooms (BYOD model); APS Technology Task Force researched for 2 years prior; plan to expand district-wide to all middle school then HS; Chromebooks now required for 6-12
1:1 Device Initiative provides Chromebooks for school and home use; Chromebook team set up 3,000+ devices summer 2022; COVID-era distribution 2020-21; no pre-2020 launch year confirmed
District has educational technology and AUP for district-provided technology resources; no specific 1:1 launch year found; upper bound 2020
Grades 6-8 provided Chromebook to take home starting 2018-2019 SY; HS also 1:1; elementary grades 3+ also 1:1 per digital learning plan
Enlarged City School District of Middletown; no specific 1:1 launch year found; upper bound 2020
Caldwell had 1-to-1 student to device system prior to COVID (per Apr 2020 article); secondary schools distributed hundreds of Chromebooks; upper bound pre-2020
Grades 7-12 Dell laptops for school and home; grades 2-6 classroom Dell laptops; grades K-1 iPads; district is Dell EMC Model School; no specific launch year found
COVID-era distribution spring 2020; ~350 elementary students at Frank Wagner ES received Chromebooks; prior to full 1:1 many students lacked home computers; technology levy supported district
100% of Northwest students issued Chromebook; district uses Google Workspace; students take device home nightly; no specific launch year found in web sources
Floyd County Schools uses Dell 2-in-1 3100 Chromebook; 1:1 initiative provides devices for school and home; tech helpline launched Sept 2020; no specific pre-2020 launch year found
District has been 1:1 since 2011 (per 2016 article); transitioned from MacBook Air to Chromebook K-12 in summer 2016; project completed before 2016-17 SY start
Announced all classes online Aug 2020; each student received Chromebook for remote learning; COVID-driven 1:1 rollout; district had existing tech infrastructure (450+ classrooms)
All students grades 4-12 provided Chromebook to take home daily starting 2019-20 SY; per 1:1 Chromebook Initiative page on district site
District has Chromebook program; no specific pre-2020 launch year found in web sources; upper bound 2020
SRCS IT Services provides Chromebook support; 2016-19 Technology Standard Roadmap noted; no specific 1:1 launch year confirmed; upper bound 2020
Grades 6-8 iPad; grades 9-12 MacBook; required $50 annual usage fee; 1:1 FAQ page exists; no specific launch year found; upper bound 2020

1:1 project started 2014-2015 SY; first sent devices home 2015-16; initially iPads then shifted to Chromebooks; ACLU MA public records (Nov 2014) identified district as running 1:1; middle school 6th grade Chromebook presentation noted
All MCAS students K-12 issued school-owned Chromebook or tablet; take home daily or on limited basis; optional $30 insurance for 7-12; no specific launch year found
Chromebooks for grades 3-12; iPads for TK-2; selected for ease of use and portability; no specific launch year found in web sources; upper bound 2020
District part of Digital Promise league; 1:1 Chromebook and tablet initiatives referenced; blended learning model with cloud-based curriculum; no specific launch year confirmed
Johnston HS became 1:1 iPad school in 2012 (one of first large HS in Iowa); JMS grades 8-9 in 2015; Summit MS grades 6-7 in 2016; elementary completed 2020; Apple Distinguished District 2024
Grades 6-12 assigned Chromebooks; PreK-5 classroom sets only; incoming 6th graders and freshman assigned at registration; no specific launch year found
District website and basic program exist; CA distance learning devices distributed 2020; no specific 1:1 program launch year found in web sources
TCPS prepared for 1:1 initiative; 3,700 new devices arrived at technology hub; goal to have device per student after Christmas break (early Jan 2021); COVID-era full deployment
District provides Chromebooks to students while school is in session; 2,700 Chromebooks via Operation Connectivity 2020; no pre-2020 launch year found
MBMS (grades 6-8) Chromebook Program 2019-20 form found on district site; indicates program in place by 2019-20 SY; middle school initial rollout

Murray City SD funded one of Utah's first 1:1 programs in 2018; every student assigned laptop (largely Chromebooks); smooth COVID transition in March 2020 due to existing 1:1 infrastructure; district built own LTE network 2021
One to World Learning initiative; full 1:1 for grades 9-12 starting Fall 2017; middle schools had classroom carts from 2014; HS partial carts from 2015-16; grades 1 5 9 get new device
District has 11 schools; Facebook page exists; no specific 1:1 program launch year found in web sources; upper bound 2020

Muskogee Public Schools 1:1 program with Google Chromebooks; T-Mobile EmpowerED hotspot rollout announced Dec 2018; each student gets Chromebook and hotspot; Pure Storage infrastructure case study references existing program
All HS students can check out Chromebook for school and home; district making strides equipping students; buses equipped with Wi-Fi; no specific firm launch year found
